description: Breathing exercise scripts for Calm Quest — guided breathing and relaxation exercises

exercises.title: 4-7-8 Breathing
exercises.subtitle: The Relaxing Breath
script_steps: Find a comfortable seated position and close your eyes.
Place the tip of your tongue behind your upper front teeth and keep it there throughout the exercise.
Exhale completely through your mouth, making a whoosh sound.
Close your mouth and inhale quietly through your nose for a count of 4.
Hold your breath for a count of 7.
Exhale completely through your mouth with a whoosh sound for a count of 8.
This completes one breath cycle. Repeat three more times.
As you practice, let each exhale be a complete release of tension.
Your mind may wander — that's okay. Simply return your focus to the count.
exercises.closing: Gently open your eyes. Notice how calm and relaxed your body feels.

exercises.title: Box Breathing
exercises.subtitle: Square Breathing — The Navy SEAL Technique
script_steps: Sit up tall with your shoulders relaxed and both feet flat on the floor.
Close your eyes or soften your gaze.
Visualize a square in your mind. Each side represents a count of four.
Inhale slowly through your nose for a count of 4 — travel up the first side of the square.
Hold your breath for a count of 4 — travel across the top of the square.
Exhale slowly through your mouth for a count of 4 — travel down the right side.
Hold your lungs empty for a count of 4 — travel across the bottom of the square.
You have completed one side of the square. Continue for four more rounds.
Let each breath be smooth and even — like the sides of a perfect square.
If you lose count, simply start again at the next breath.
exercises.closing: When you're ready, release the visualization and take one natural breath. Notice the stillness within you.

exercises.title: Simple Deep Breathing
exercises.subtitle: Belly Breathing Basics
script_steps: Find a comfortable position — lying down is wonderful for this exercise.
Place one hand on your belly and one hand on your chest.
Without changing your breath, just notice which hand rises more as you breathe.
Now begin to breathe deeply into your belly, feeling your lower hand rise with each inhale.
Inhale slowly through your nose for a count of 4, letting your belly fill like a balloon.
Pause gently at the top of your breath.
Exhale slowly through your mouth for a count of 6, feeling your belly fall.
Let your exhale be longer than your inhale — this activates your relaxation response.
With each exhale, imagine releasing any tension you're holding.
Continue for six deep, nourishing breaths.
exercises.closing: Release your hands to your sides. Take one natural breath. Notice how your body has softened.

exercises.title: Progressive Muscle Relaxation
exercises.subtitle: Release Tension Throughout Your Body
script_steps: Lie down or sit comfortably with your arms uncrossed and legs uncrossed.
Close your eyes and take three deep, grounding breaths.
We will systematically tense and release each muscle group. Tense for 5 seconds, then release for 10.
Begin with your feet — curl your toes tightly, hold, and release. Feel the difference between tension and relaxation.
Move to your calves — flex your feet upward, feel the pull in your calves, hold, and release.
Now your thighs — squeeze your thigh muscles tight, hold, and let them soften completely.
Tense your abdomen by pulling your belly button toward your spine. Hold and release.
Clench your hands into fists. Squeeze tightly, hold, and let them fall open.
Tense your arms — bend at the elbows and make a muscle. Hold and release, letting your arms fall heavy.
Shrug your shoulders up toward your ears as high as you can. Hold the tension and release with a sigh.
Tense your face — scrunch your eyes, clench your jaw, squeeze everything tight. Hold and release completely.
Now take a full-body scan. Breathe into any remaining tightness and let it dissolve.
exercises.closing: Lie still for a moment. Feel the weight of your fully relaxed body. Notice how light and calm you feel.

exercises.title: Body Scan Meditation
exercises.subtitle: Full Awareness Journey
script_steps: Lie down on your back with your arms at your sides, palms facing up.
Close your eyes and take three slow, settling breaths.
Bring your awareness to the top of your head. Notice any sensations — warmth, tingling, or simply the presence of your scalp.
Slowly move your attention to your forehead and eyes. Notice if they feel tight or soft. Let them soften.
Bring awareness to your jaw — this is a common place to hold tension. Let your jaw drop slightly, teeth apart.
Move your awareness down to your neck and throat. Breathe into any tightness here.
Notice your shoulders — are they lifted or relaxed? Imagine them melting into the floor.
Bring attention to your arms, moving down to your elbows, forearms, wrists, and fingertips. Notice the energy flowing through.
Shift your awareness to your chest and upper back. Feel the gentle rise and fall with each breath.
Bring attention to your abdomen. Notice it expanding and contracting naturally.
Move to your lower back and hips. Imagine your breath flowing into this area, softening it.
Bring awareness to your thighs, knees, calves, and all the way down to your feet.
Feel your toes — wiggle them slightly. Feel your feet making contact with the ground.
Now expand your awareness to your entire body — a complete field of sensation from head to toe.
Rest here for a few more breaths, feeling whole and present.
exercises.closing: Slowly begin to wiggle your fingers and toes. Gently roll to one side and rest for a moment before coming to sit.

exercises.title: Ocean Breath
exercises.subtitle: Ujjayi Pranayama — The Victorious Breath
script_steps: Sit comfortably with your spine tall and your shoulders relaxed.
Close your eyes and bring your awareness to your breath without changing it.
Take a deep inhale through your nose. As you exhale, open your mouth and make a 'HAAAH' sound — like you're fogging up a mirror.
Try again: exhale with that 'HAAAH' sound, feeling the breath pass through your throat.
Now close your mouth. Inhale and exhale through your nose while gently constricting the back of your throat.
The sound should resemble ocean waves — a soft, steady 'sssss' sound on the inhale and 'hhhhh' on the exhale.
If it helps, imagine you're trying to whisper the sound 'AH' with your mouth closed.
Find a steady rhythm: inhale for 4 counts with the ocean sound, exhale for 6 counts with the ocean sound.
Let your breath be smooth and continuous — like waves rolling onto shore and receding back.
Continue for 10 full breaths, letting each wave of breath carry you deeper into calm.
If your throat feels strained, soften the constriction. The sound should be gentle and effortless.
exercises.closing: Release the throat constriction and return to your natural breath. Notice the calm and spaciousness within you.
